acceptance_criteria.criterion: `ModelEntrySchema` validates entries with UUID `id`, non-empty `name`, slug matching `/^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/`, and `cc_model` defaulting to `"inherit"`
`readModels()` auto-initializes `local.json` from `default.json` when `local.json` does not exist, and returns the 4 default entries
`writeModels()` rejects duplicate slugs with a validation error
`writeModels()` rejects the reserved slug `"inherit"` on non-sentinel entries (entries whose UUID is not `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`)
`writeModels()` rejects deletion of models whose UUID is referenced in `assignments.json`, returning usage details
Slug renames via `writeModels()` leave `assignments.json` unchanged — assignment values are stable UUIDs, unaffected by slug changes
`loadDefaults()` adds entries from `default.json` whose `id` is not already in `local.json` and preserves existing entries
`loadDefaults()` detects slug collisions between default and local entries and returns them as `conflicts`
`readAssignments()` returns a default structure (`{ default_model_uuid: undefined, persona_models: {} }`) when `assignments.json` does not exist
`getResolvedAssignments()` resolves UUID values to slugs using `local.json` and omits persona entries with unresolvable UUIDs (graceful degradation)

summary: Implemented `mcp-server/src/gui/model-registry.ts` with all required public functions and schemas, and `mcp-server/tests/gui/model-registry.test.ts` covering all 13 acceptance criteria. All 47 unit tests pass; no regressions in adjacent test files.

comments.note: model-registry.ts internally calls readModels() inside writeModels() to build the 'existing models' set for deletion detection. This incurs a second filesystem read on every write. A future optimization could accept an optional `previousModels` parameter to allow callers that already hold the registry in memory to skip the re-read. For the current usage pattern (API handler reads then writes in the same request) this is negligible but worth noting.

The _initializeLocalFromDefault() helper is prefixed with a single underscore to signal 'internal only'. The codebase has no established convention for internal helpers (config.ts uses `isNodeError` unprefixed). Aligning to a consistent convention across modules would help new contributors. Since the function is unexported, the underscore is purely documentary.

loadDefaults() currently returns the full merged array including pre-existing local entries as `models`, but only writes to disk when toAdd.length > 0. If the caller re-renders the registry from the returned models array while the disk write is in flight (async), there's a theoretical TOCTOU window. In practice this is fine since the GUI operates sequentially, but a comment noting the write condition would clarify intent.

comments.note: AC-1 slug regex /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ — verified boundary conditions: trailing hyphen, leading hyphen, consecutive hyphens (all rejected), single alphanumeric (accepted). Implementation is correct.

loadDefaults() early-return path: when toAdd.length === 0 AND conflicts.length === 0, returns { models: locals, conflicts: [] } without a disk write. Correct behavior — idempotent re-invocation is safe.

getResolvedAssignments() — gracefully handles both missing assignments.json AND missing/unreadable local.json, returning { default_model_slug: null, persona_models: {} } in both cases. Edge-case verified with QA test.

writeModels() calls readModels() internally during the deletion guard phase (step 4). If local.json does not exist at all, the code catches all errors and treats existingModels as []. However, if local.json exists but has a schema validation error, the error is silently swallowed too (empty catch in writeModels). This means a corrupted local.json would allow a write to proceed as if it were empty, potentially bypassing the deletion guard. Consider narrowing the catch to ENOENT-only errors, similar to how readModels() handles it. Not a blocker for current AC, but a latent risk.
No issues with the vi.mock scoping — the mock redirects WORKSPACE_ROOT to a per-test temp directory and is properly cleaned up in afterEach. No test-isolation leakage observed.

summary: Code review FAIL — one blocking issue: writeModels() uses a bare `catch {}` (lines 202–207) that swallows ALL errors from readModels() during the deletion guard phase. A corrupted local.json (PARSE_ERROR or VALIDATION_ERROR from readModels) silently falls through to existingModels=[], making deletedModels empty and bypassing the deletion guard entirely. The module's documented guarantee — 'rejects deletion of models whose UUID is referenced in assignments.json' — is violated when local.json is corrupted. Fix: narrow the catch to ENOENT-only by re-throwing ApiError exceptions, analogous to the readModels() pattern at line 113–116. One fix-forward comment applied to loadDefaults() clarifying the dead-code path in its readModels catch block.

comments.note: [BLOCKING] writeModels() deletion guard catch (lines 202–207): the bare `catch {}` swallows ALL errors thrown by readModels() — including ApiError PARSE_ERROR and VALIDATION_ERROR — treating them identically to ENOENT. With existingModels=[], deletedModels is always empty, so the deletion guard never fires. A caller that submits a new model list while local.json is corrupt will silently succeed even when it is deleting models referenced in assignments.json. FIX: replace the bare catch with a targeted re-throw for ApiError, keeping only the ENOENT-equivalent silent path. Pattern to follow (same file, readModels line 113): `if (isNodeError(err) && err.code === 'ENOENT') { ... } else { throw err; }`. For readModels(), the ENOENT case comes back as the ApiError wrapping is done after the catch — in writeModels(), readModels() is called directly, so throw any ApiError through: `try { existingModels = await readModels(); } catch (err) { if (!(err instanceof ApiError && err.code === 'READ_ERROR') && !(isNodeError(err) && err.code === 'ENOENT')) throw err; }`

[Fix-Forward applied] loadDefaults() readModels catch block (line 346–353): the comment said 'local.json doesn\'t exist — treat as empty' but this is misleading — the ENOENT case is handled inside readModels() via auto-init and never reaches this catch as READ_ERROR. The block is actually handling non-ENOENT OS errors (e.g. permission denied) on local.json. Also, VALIDATION_ERROR and PARSE_ERROR were not explicitly re-thrown here (the `else { throw err; }` branch handles it, but no comment clarified why). Updated the comment to accurately describe what each error code path means and why READ_ERROR is silently absorbed while other ApiErrors are re-thrown. No behavioral change.

The _initializeLocalFromDefault() function uses a single-underscore prefix to signal 'internal only'. config.ts uses `isNodeError` without any prefix. Consider aligning to a single convention across the gui/ module (e.g. fully private via module closure, or a consistent `_` prefix). Since the function is unexported this is cosmetic, but worth standardizing for new contributors.

[documentation-forward] writeModels() JSDoc (lines 143–158) documents the deletion guard behavior but does not mention what happens when local.json does not yet exist (guard is skipped, write proceeds). Once the ENOENT narrowing fix is applied, also document what happens when local.json exists but is corrupt (write is now rejected with ApiError). Updating the `@throws` block and guard description in the JSDoc would make the function contract explicit for future API handler authors.

loadDefaults() writes to disk only when toAdd.length > 0, but returns the merged array regardless. If the caller re-renders the UI from the returned models before the disk write completes (async), there is a brief TOCTOU window. A comment noting 'disk write is conditional on toAdd.length > 0; the returned models array always reflects the full merge' would clarify intent. (Developer noted this; confirming it warrants a comment rather than a structural change.)
